descriptionChirho: The plural noun tseva'ot meaning 'hosts' or 'armies', overwhelmingly used in the divine epithet YHWH Tseva'ot ('LORD of Hosts'). S129412 covers the vast majority of occurrences (284x) with article-prefixed and construct forms, while S129415 covers 2 instances in a more general 'armies' usage. Despite the slight contextual variation, all multilingual glosses converge on the same lexeme: eng 'hosts/armies', spa 'ejercitos', hin सेनाओं, arb جُنُود, kor 만군/군대, swa 'majeshi'. This is a single lexical sense — 'hosts/armies' — whether in the divine title or in rare non-titular usage.
